g.text: The Costas loop as a control system
A phase-locked loop whose phase detector ignores 180° flips. Numbers from sim/budget.py section 6; the plots are the textbook second-order loop with these numbers.
PI: (1 + s R2 C) / (s R1 C)
LO phase θ_o back to the demodulator (the 'minus' input: error = θ_i - θ_o)

path.style: fill: #fffbe6; stroke: #999988; stroke-width: 0.6; stroke-linejoin: miter

g.text: zero at 0 AND at 180°: a BPSK flip is invisible

path.style: fill: #fffbe6; stroke: #999988; stroke-width: 0.6; stroke-linejoin: miter

g.text: slews at most ±580 kHz of LO

path.style: fill: #fffbe6; stroke: #999988; stroke-width: 0.6; stroke-linejoin: miter

g.text: Open loop: G(s) = K_d · F(s) · K_o / s
with F(s) = (1 + s τ2) / (s τ1), τ1 = R1 C = 945 µs, τ2 = R2 C = 75 µs
Closed loop (second order): ω_n = sqrt(K_d K_o / τ1) = 2π · 3000 Hz, ζ = ω_n τ2 / 2 = 0.70
• 3 kHz: the loop corrects phase in ~100 µs, follows oscillator drift and the TCXO offset (29 kHz, inside the ±580 kHz pull),
and is 30,000 times slower than a 10 ns symbol, so the symbols do not move it.
• Hold range ±580 kHz (the VCXO's pull); pull-in from anywhere inside it, in ~ (Δf)² / ω_n³ … a few ms at worst.
• Phase noise of the LO inside 3 kHz is cleaned up by the loop (it follows the far carrier); outside, it is the MAX2871's own (-109 dBc/Hz in-band, 80 kHz PLL).
• Lock is 0° or 180°: both are stable; the data appears inverted in one of them. The gateware defines 'idle' = the level it sees after lock, and an event is a change.
the detector's S-curve: stable at 0 and ±π

path.style: fill: #eef7ee; stroke: #77aa77; stroke-width: 0.6; stroke-linejoin: miter

g.text: Why a Costas loop and not a plain PLL: a PLL on a BPSK signal sees the carrier flip 180° at every bit and loses lock. The Costas detector multiplies the Q arm by the SIGN of the I arm:
flipping the carrier flips both, so the product does not change. Here the multiplication is an analogue switch (74LVC1G3157) selecting +Q or -Q under the comparator's sign(I): a 'hard-limited'
Costas loop, the cheapest and the one whose S-curve is drawn above. The loop filter is a PI (proportional + integral): the integral term drives the steady-state phase error to zero even with
a frequency offset (the TCXO's 29 kHz). The HOLD switch opens the integrator's input when the FPGA knows the carrier is absent (our own TX in T/R mode): VC stays where it was and the LO
coasts on the VCXO's stability (1e-9 over a microsecond = 6 Hz: nothing). LOOP_SEL = FPGA turns the detector into a plain Q-only PLL, for comparison in the lab.
